manifest.title: Warmbly
manifest.author: Marcus Quinn <marcus@marcusquinn.com>
manifest.description:
Warmbly is an open-source platform for B2B cold outreach and email warmup:
multi-step campaigns across many mailboxes, a unified inbox for every reply,
a CRM, and the deliverability tooling that keeps those mailboxes out of spam.

### Features

* **Campaigns:** multi-step sequences with per-mailbox caps and spacing.
* **Unified inbox:** every connected mailbox and reply in one place.
* **CRM:** contacts, pipelines, deals, tasks and meetings.
* **Warmup:** a monitored pool of real mailboxes.
* **Deliverability:** bounces, complaints, suppression lists and open/click
  tracking on your own tracking domain.
* **Hosted forms:** lead-capture pages and embeds.
* **Automations:** visual reply playbooks, with optional AI steps using your
  own provider key.
* **Integrations:** HubSpot, Pipedrive, Slack, Zapier, REST API and webhooks.
* **Realtime:** live presence and updates across the team.

### Cloudron integration

* **Single sign-on:** Cloudron users can sign in with their Cloudron account.
* **Outgoing mail:** sign-in codes, password resets and invitations go
  through the Cloudron mail relay.
* **Own domains:** the dashboard, API, admin panel, tracking and forms each
  get a domain with a Cloudron certificate. Add customers' tracking domains
  as aliases of the app.
* **Backups:** the PostgreSQL database, stored files and the encryption keys
  are in Cloudron backups.

The whole self-host stack (API, event consumer, mailbox worker, tracking,
forms, realtime gateway and NATS) runs in one container on Cloudron's
PostgreSQL and Redis. No cloud account is needed.

[Warmbly](https://github.com/warmbly/warmbly) is open source under the
Apache-2.0 licence. This package is maintained independently of the Warmbly
project.
manifest.tagline: Open-source B2B cold outreach and email warmup

API_DOMAIN.title: API domain
API_DOMAIN.description: API, unsubscribe links, OAuth callbacks and the realtime socket

TRACK_DOMAIN.title: Tracking domain
TRACK_DOMAIN.description: Open and click tracking in campaign mail

manifest.postInstallMessage:
Warmbly is starting. The first start runs the database migrations and can
take a few minutes.

<sso>
**Claim the instance:** open the app and choose **Continue with** your
Cloudron on the sign-in screen; no email or password is needed. The first
person to sign in becomes the owner and platform admin. Later Cloudron
users with access to this app get an ordinary account on their first sign-in.
Set `OIDC_DEFAULT_ORG` in `/app/data/env` to the organization id they should
join; without it each new user gets their own organization.
</sso>
<nosso>
**Claim the instance.** In the app's **Terminal**, run:

    warmblyctl setup-link

Open the link it prints and create the owner account and organization. The
link is single-use; run the command again for a fresh one.
</nosso>

Cloudron sign-in needs no invitation: the app's **Access control** decides
which Cloudron users can sign in (set `SSO_AUTO_PROVISION=false` in
`/app/data/env` to require invitations for them too). Password sign-ups need
an invitation (`DISABLE_REGISTRATION=invite_only`), and are closed until the
owner has claimed the instance. Invite the team from the dashboard.

The admin panel is on the **Admin domain** you chose. Customers' own tracking
domains (a CNAME to your tracking domain) need adding as aliases of this app
so Cloudron issues their certificates.

Settings live in `/app/data/env`. Keep backups: `/app/data/.secrets.env`
holds the keys that decrypt connected mailbox credentials.

Setup guide: [README](https://github.com/marcusquinn/cloudron-warmbly-app/blob/main/README.md).
manifest.changelog:
* Initial package of Warmbly 0.6.70.
* Single container: API, event consumer, mailbox worker, tracking, hosted forms, realtime gateway and NATS JetStream under supervisord, on Cloudron PostgreSQL and Redis.
* Separate domains for the API, admin panel, tracking and forms; the realtime socket runs through the API domain.
* Cloudron single sign-on (OIDC): a Cloudron user's first sign-in creates their account.
* The first Cloudron sign-in on a new instance becomes its owner and platform admin; no setup link needed (`WARMBLY_OIDC_FIRST_USER_OWNER`). Until then, password, Apple and Google sign-ups are refused, so nobody can take the instance first.
* The sign-in screen offers "Continue with" your Cloudron straight away, without typing an email first, and says when the first sign-in will claim the instance.
* Platform email through the Cloudron mail relay.
* Customer tracking domains can be added as app aliases.
* `warmblyctl` in the web terminal runs the upstream operator CLI (`setup-link`, `status`, `user`, `backup`).

* Retain the Cloudron first-owner sign-in patch and the pinned Cloudron 6.0.1 base.

manifest.title: Warmbly
manifest.author: Marcus Quinn <marcus@marcusquinn.com>
manifest.description:
Warmbly is an open-source platform for B2B cold outreach and email warmup:
multi-step campaigns across many mailboxes, a unified inbox for every reply,
a CRM, and the deliverability tooling that keeps those mailboxes out of spam.

### Features

* **Campaigns:** multi-step sequences with per-mailbox caps and spacing.
* **Unified inbox:** every connected mailbox and reply in one place.
* **CRM:** contacts, pipelines, deals, tasks and meetings.
* **Warmup:** a monitored pool of real mailboxes.
* **Deliverability:** bounces, complaints, suppression lists and open/click
  tracking on your own tracking domain.
* **Hosted forms:** lead-capture pages and embeds.
* **Automations:** visual reply playbooks, with optional AI steps using your
  own provider key.
* **Integrations:** HubSpot, Pipedrive, Slack, Zapier, REST API and webhooks.
* **Realtime:** live presence and updates across the team.

### Cloudron integration

* **Single sign-on:** Cloudron users can sign in with their Cloudron account.
* **Outgoing mail:** sign-in codes, password resets and invitations go
  through the Cloudron mail relay.
* **Own domains:** the dashboard, API, admin panel, tracking and forms each
  get a domain with a Cloudron certificate. Add customers' tracking domains
  as aliases of the app.
* **Backups:** the PostgreSQL database, stored files and the encryption keys
  are in Cloudron backups.

The whole self-host stack (API, event consumer, mailbox worker, tracking,
forms, realtime gateway and NATS) runs in one container on Cloudron's
PostgreSQL and Redis. No cloud account is needed.

[Warmbly](https://github.com/warmbly/warmbly) is open source under the
Apache-2.0 licence. This package is maintained independently of the Warmbly
project.

manifest.postInstallMessage:
Warmbly is starting. The first start runs the database migrations and can
take a few minutes.

<sso>
**Claim the instance:** open the app and choose **Continue with** your
Cloudron on the sign-in screen; no email or password is needed. The first
person to sign in becomes the owner and platform admin. Later Cloudron
users with access to this app get an ordinary account on their first sign-in.
Set `OIDC_DEFAULT_ORG` in `/app/data/env` to the organization id they should
join; without it each new user gets their own organization.
</sso>
<nosso>
**Claim the instance.** In the app's **Terminal**, run:

    warmblyctl setup-link

Open the link it prints and create the owner account and organization. The
link is single-use; run the command again for a fresh one.
</nosso>

Cloudron sign-in needs no invitation: the app's **Access control** decides
which Cloudron users can sign in (set `SSO_AUTO_PROVISION=false` in
`/app/data/env` to require invitations for them too). Password sign-ups need
an invitation (`DISABLE_REGISTRATION=invite_only`), and are closed until the
owner has claimed the instance. Invite the team from the dashboard.

The admin panel is on the **Admin domain** you chose. Customers' own tracking
domains (a CNAME to your tracking domain) need adding as aliases of this app
so Cloudron issues their certificates.

Settings live in `/app/data/env`. Keep backups: `/app/data/.secrets.env`
holds the keys that decrypt connected mailbox credentials.

Setup guide: [README](https://github.com/marcusquinn/cloudron-warmbly-app/blob/main/README.md).
manifest.changelog:
* Update Warmbly to 0.7.2 at upstream commit 7af95ad, with release image digests pinned from upstream's images.json.
* Lead finder: search a map for businesses (OpenStreetMap by default, no key needed), enrich them with website emails and add them to contacts (upstream 0.7.0).
* Per-campaign ramp-up, sending in each lead's local time, region segments, warmup recipients balanced by provider, and shared notifications sent as one digest (upstream 0.7.2).
* Typed mailbox send pauses, better bounce accuracy, opt-in per-step inbox rotation and client roles for restricted members (upstream 0.7.0).
* Gmail mailboxes connected with your own Google OAuth client now ask for full mail access (https://mail.google.com/) so warmup can run over IMAP; add that scope to the client's consent screen. The dashboard offers Google sign-in whenever the backend allows it (upstream 0.7.0).
* IMAP folder cursors work with NetEase servers (upstream 0.7.1).
* Retain the Cloudron first-owner sign-in patch and the pinned Cloudron 6.0.1 base.

manifest.changelog:
* Update Warmbly to 0.7.3 at upstream commit 443b6c8, with release image digests pinned from upstream's images.json.
* Lead finder falls back to a reader and web search for sites that turn it away; warmup hides other services' mail, with an opt-in warmup filter tag (upstream 0.7.3).
* A cancelled scheduled email is never sent, interrupted manual sends are settled, and Idempotency-Key records are tied to the credential and resource (upstream 0.7.3).
* `warmblyctl backup` and `restore` match the PostgreSQL client to the server, and restore is transactional; integration credentials are carried in workspace archives (upstream 0.7.3).
* Retain the Cloudron first-owner sign-in patch and the pinned Cloudron 6.0.1 base.
